title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 68
paragraphs: This too is additional proof to me that all the fortunes of the barbarians depended on the Persians — namely that at that time these men fled before they had even engaged the enemy, because they saw the Persians doing so. Thus all were in flight except only the cavalry, including that of the Boeotians; and this rendered a service to the fugitives by constantly staying close to the enemy and keeping their own side's fugitives separated from the Greeks.
